correctness.rationale: For any direction, orthogonal projection removes its squared row correlation. Averaging the maximum of two distinct sampled correlations gives F_m=1/2+[m(m−1)]^(-1) Σ_{i<j}|r_i−r_j| from the tight-frame identity. Each correlation crossing lies on an angular half-grid, and between crossings F_m is strictly concave, hence every minimizer lies on the grid. There are precisely two symmetry classes: aligned and bisector; order-statistic sums and explicit finite geometric-series derivatives yield the odd/even values and the exact even orientation gap. Strict concavity excludes other minimizers. Conditional expectation iterates, with no asymptotic equality claimed. Reproducible Python checker enumerates all pairs for m=3..74, 7,200 angle probes and asymptotics. Numerical enumeration is supplementary, not proof.

evidence: De Loera, Haddock and Needell (arXiv:1605.01418) establishes the broader algorithm, and Haddock and Ma (arXiv:1912.03544) gives improved convergence guarantees without this exact constant.

originality.rationale: The original algorithms, exact regular planar frame and uniform single-row factor are preexisting. The additional claimed exact best-of-two, without-replacement mean-square minimax constant for every integer m≥3, its odd/even minimizers and explicit quartic alignment penalty were compared against inspected primary algorithm results, the directly matching frame textbook example, and searched published mathematical findings. None was found to assert or strongly imply the combined exact statement. This is a qualified priority judgment, not proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: The classic SKM setting uses a budget of two residual evaluations per projection; one-step expected squared-error progress controls a uniform convergence bound. The natural finite unit harmonic frames are a canonical geometry with known single-probe contraction exactly 1/2, so the exact benefit of a two-row greedy choice is mathematically motivated rather than an arbitrary small-instance enumeration. The theorem covers every frame size, exhibits a nontrivial odd/even extremizer bifurcation and gives a sharp orientation penalty of order m^-4, enabling exact benchmarks for sampling analyses. It does not pretend to be an optimal runtime result or a general-matrix theorem.
